title: Funchal on Madeira becomes a town of the crown: the empire's first settlement beyond the sea, 1,800 souls, peasants and slaves, Castilian by tongue and Muslim by faith

data.note: owned from 1 January 1412 by the save's ownership record; with the island settlements a new estate, the tribes, appears (Trent), to be followed only once it holds 3–4% of power or more

title: Jadīla bint Saʿd, the heir's young wife and sister of the Shaykha of Qūnka, takes a fifth seat in the dīwān, set to drawing settlers to the realm

The age of the spice trade. Word comes that a sea road to the Indies has been found, and pepper and cinnamon are worth more than ever. Ishbīliya and al-Ushbūna are among the seven markets of the West that become ports of the spice trade, with Genoa, Constantinople, Barcelona, Bordeaux and Naples

data.event: Spice Trade: the discovery of the East Indian Trade Route has ushered in the age of the Spice Trade; with new trade routes available, controlling the flow of spices like pepper or cinnamon has become more important than ever (the game's text)

effects.markets: Spice Trade for 20 years in the markets of Genoa, Constantinople, Barcelona, Ishbīliya, Bordeaux, Naples and al-Ushbūna

data.note: who found the route is not on the screen

title: Maryam bint Yūsuf, daughter of Yūsuf I and the ablest mind of the dīwān for a generation, dies at fifty-five. Her seat passes to Aḥmad ibn Yūsuf, grandson of her brother Ismāʿīl
Khālid ibn Yaḥyā Raḥḥū, general of the Marīnid war, captain of the prospectors, victor of Granadilla and first lord of Burghush, dies at sixty-nine. His son Abū Ḥammū succeeds him in Burghush
